bsig_watch.why_exponential: Google put its first AI-chip satellite into orbit on October 1, a test of running compute on solar power in space, while the power a single US campus draws became public by accident.
bsig_watch.watch: Google says the Project Suncatcher prototype launched with Planet on SpaceX's Transporter-18 and is 'operating as expected', with data to come over the coming weeks. Watch whether the orbital test reports power and heat figures, and whether more states force data-centre usage into the open.
bsig_watch.expressions: Constellation, Vistra, Cameco, and other power and nuclear operators.

bsig_watch.trend: Open weights close the gap by compression
bsig_watch.why_exponential: Quantisation is now doing what new architectures used to: prism-ml's Bonsai 2 27B stores its weights as minus one, zero or plus one at about 1.75 bits each, fits in 5.95 gigabytes and keeps 98.2 percent of the full-precision Qwen3.8 27B's aggregate benchmark score on prism-ml's own suite, which reports about 130 tokens a second on an RTX 5090.
bsig_watch.watch: A set of 2- and 3-bit builds of the 125-billion-parameter Qwen3.8-Flash-Next reached 2,244,732 thirty-day downloads as the Strata engine ran it on a 12-gigabyte gaming card, and Bonsai 2's ternary build rose to 4,120,718. Watch whether a frontier lab answers with a model sized for a consumer GPU.
bsig_watch.expressions: Consumer GPUs, Apple silicon, and the open-weight download curve.

bsig_watch.trend: Inference costs reverse toward custom silicon
bsig_watch.why_exponential: Memory, not logic, is now the scarce input: on September 30 Micron reported record quarterly revenue of $54.23 billion, against $11.32 billion a year earlier, and said more than 75 percent of its 2027 output is already committed.
bsig_watch.watch: Micron expects memory supply-demand conditions to be 'much tighter in calendar 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026' and has no 'line of sight' to balance. Watch whether server makers keep shipping machines with less memory per server, and whether the labs' $2 and $10 list price survives the end of Google's introductory Argon price.
bsig_watch.expressions: AMD, Marvell, Broadcom, Samsung, and SK Hynix.

bsig_watch.why_exponential: Governments are now ordering compute at national scale, including Saudi Arabia's 2,200-megawatt HUMAIN project, the European Union's planned gigafactories and India's 100,000-GPU programme, and some have moved on to commissioning open-weight models of their own rather than only buying hardware.
bsig_watch.watch: Aleph Alpha released Kolibri on October 3, a 78-billion-parameter open-weight model trained on 768 Nvidia B200s in Germany and Finland, 'under European and German law, with no foreign control'. Watch whether European governments buy it or only praise it.
bsig_watch.expressions: Nvidia, national AI programmes, and state-commissioned open models.

bsig_watch.why_exponential: Leverage in crypto futures and stablecoin dry powder swing sharply, and extreme readings often precede reversals.
bsig_watch.watch: Bitcoin ended the week flat at about $84,500 while the dollar rose. On October 5 the CFTC opened comment on an advance notice of rules for leveraged retail crypto trading, including a new exchange registration category for it. Watch funding rates and the comment period.
bsig_watch.expressions: Bitcoin, Ether, and Coinbase.

bsig_watch.why_exponential: Droughts ripple through several steps before they reach markets, and each step tends to amplify the one before it. The chain is now visible in prices, but running backwards: the current harvest is arriving in volume while forecasters cut the next one.
bsig_watch.watch: Ivory Coast shipments to ports reached 2.14 million tonnes in the marketing year to September 13, up 18 percent, and ICE inventories hit a two-year high, so cocoa fell 10.2 percent even as early surveys put the 2026/27 Ivory Coast crop at 1.8 million tonnes, down 18 percent. Papua New Guinea has 2.4 million people affected by El Nino frost and drought. Watch NOAA's October 8 update against the new crop.
bsig_watch.expressions: Cocoa, coffee, grains, and water-stressed producers.

bsig_watch.why_exponential: Apps and services increasingly demand cryptographic proof that a device runs trusted, unmodified software before they will run at all, and the state is starting to ask for the same signal.
bsig_watch.watch: GrapheneOS reported on September 16 that Android 17 QPR1, released the day before, is the first Android release since 3.x to add new developer APIs without a matching release to the Android Open Source Project, which leaves alternative builds tracking a target they cannot see. Google says the code reaches AOSP with QPR2 in December. Watch whether that commitment holds.
bsig_watch.expressions: GrapheneOS, Google Play Integrity, and age-verification law.

bsig_watch.why_exponential: Frontier labs are moving from software into laboratories and medical hardware, which changes both their capital needs and their regulators.
bsig_watch.watch: Anthropic confirmed on September 18 that it runs a Bay Area wet lab, without disclosing its opening date, size or biosafety level, and said it is not specifically for drug discovery. Watch for the first device clearance sought by a frontier lab rather than a medical-device company.
bsig_watch.expressions: Anthropic, Midjourney, large pharma, and gene-editing firms.

bsig_watch.why_exponential: The AI buildout is increasingly funded outside company books, through vehicles that issue debt and lease compute, and each layer of guarantees lets the next project borrow more.
bsig_watch.watch: Nothing new was disclosed in the week, and the test case has slipped: SB Energy, which filed on September 1 to raise $5 to $7 billion at about a $50 billion valuation on a backlog of roughly $439 billion tied largely to OpenAI leases and no operational data centres, had still not priced. Watch for a rating agency to say how much of the vehicle debt is really the sponsors' debt.
bsig_watch.expressions: Oracle, Meta, data-center debt vehicles, and Nvidia.

bsig_watch.why_exponential: As autonomous fleets scale from surface streets onto freeways, safety incidents draw their first large recalls, and regulators respond in both directions at once.
bsig_watch.watch: Nothing new during the week. Watch NHTSA recalls and freeway-service limits as fleets expand.
bsig_watch.expressions: Waymo, Tesla robotaxi, and NHTSA.

bsig_watch.why_exponential: Data-centre water use is treated as a trade secret, and the first numbers to escape show how much it varies: an improper redaction in Nebraska put Google's Lincoln campus at 13.3 million gallons a year and its Papillion site at 547.9 million.
bsig_watch.watch: The Lincoln site also showed a 52.65 megawatt peak draw, KOLN reported on September 30. Watch whether cities start requiring the figures in development agreements.
bsig_watch.expressions: European power prices, nuclear operators, and grid-interconnection queues.

glossary.note: A basis point is one hundredth of a percentage point, so 26 basis points is 0.26 percentage points.
The extra yield investors demand to hold riskier 'junk' corporate bonds instead of Treasuries. It widens when lenders get nervous, so a spread that barely moves means credit markets are calm.
The gap between ordinary and inflation-protected Treasury yields, read as the market's expected average inflation over that period.
The futures contract closest to expiry, the usual stand-in for a commodity's current price.
A prediction market whose contracts pay $1 if an event happens. A price of 80 cents means traders put the chance at roughly 80 percent.
The last price recorded before midnight Coordinated Universal Time each day, so every day is measured at the same moment.
Consumer prices excluding food and energy, which swing the most. Central banks treat it as the steadier read on underlying inflation.
The producer price index measures what businesses receive for goods and services, often an early signal for consumer prices.
The Atlanta Fed's running estimate of the current quarter's GDP growth, updated as new data arrives.
The interest rate on two-year US government debt. It moves closely with what markets expect the Fed to do.
Exchange-traded funds that hold actual bitcoin, giving investors exposure through an ordinary brokerage account.
The European Central Bank, which sets interest rates for the countries that use the euro.
The rate the ECB pays banks on overnight deposits, its main policy rate.
A Senate vote to end debate and move ahead. It needs 60 votes, which is how a filibuster is overcome.
The Strait of Hormuz, between Iran and Oman. Before the war about a fifth of the world's oil passed through it, by the US Energy Information Administration's count.
The strait between Yemen and Djibouti at the southern end of the Red Sea, on the shipping route between the Suez Canal and the Indian Ocean.
The Iran-aligned movement that controls northern Yemen, including the capital Sanaa, and has fought a Saudi-led coalition since 2015.
OPEC plus allied producers such as Russia, which coordinate oil output targets.
The International Energy Agency, a Paris-based body that publishes a monthly Oil Market Report.
A commodity-data firm that tracks tankers using satellite and ship-transponder data.
US Central Command, the military command responsible for the Middle East.
A periodic warming of the tropical Pacific that shifts weather worldwide, typically bringing drought to Indonesia and Australia and suppressing Atlantic hurricanes.
A patch of the central equatorial Pacific whose sea-surface temperature anomaly is the standard gauge of El Niño strength.
The EU's Earth-observation programme, whose climate service publishes a monthly global temperature bulletin.
The weekly US Drought Monitor map, produced by the University of Nebraska-Lincoln with NOAA and the US Department of Agriculture.
Models whose trained parameters are published for anyone to download and run, even if the training data and code are not.
Tokens are the word pieces a model reads and writes. Providers charge separately for input and for the output a model generates.
A service that routes requests to many AI models through one API and lists each model's price per million tokens.
The main hub where AI models and datasets are published and downloaded.
Seven problems named by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2000, each carrying a $1 million prize. Only the Poincaré conjecture has been confirmed solved.
Winners of the Fields Medal, awarded every four years to up to four mathematicians under 40 and often called mathematics' highest honour.
Lean is a language for writing proofs that a computer checks step by step, so a Lean-checked proof is verified by machine. People still have to confirm the formal statement matches the problem.
Automatic content recognition: software in smart TVs that identifies what is on screen to build viewing profiles for advertising.
Apple's server system for AI requests too large for the device, which Apple says processes data without keeping it.
The law Beijing imposed on Hong Kong in 2020, criminalising secession, subversion, terrorism and collusion with foreign forces.
The 2016 ruling by a tribunal under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea that rejected most of China's South China Sea claims. China does not recognise it.
A US bill setting rules for crypto markets, including how oversight divides between the SEC and the CFTC.
A technology news site run by Y Combinator where readers vote stories up. This issue counts the week's top 100 stories.

The forecasts each Federal Reserve policymaker submits four times a year for growth, unemployment, inflation and the interest rate they think appropriate. The median of the rate forecasts is often called the dot plot.
The Federal Reserve sets a quarter-point band rather than a single number for the overnight rate banks charge each other, and steers the market rate into that band.
A US prediction-market exchange regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. Its contracts settle at a dollar, so a price of 50 cents means traders put the chance at roughly 50 percent.
The share of a parliament, usually two thirds, needed to amend the constitution without votes from any other party.
The US Senate procedure for ending debate, which needs sixty votes. Failing it usually stops a bill without anyone voting on the bill itself.
A Russian mechanism, used by presidential decree since 2023, that transfers control of a foreign-owned company to a state-appointed manager while leaving formal ownership untouched.
